title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the Committee's 2020 report on AI and Public Standards by outlining new guidelines and regulatory frameworks to promote responsible AI use. It stresses transparency, accountability, public oversight, and encourages collaboration with industry to balance safety with innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, ensuring that exams and assessments remain fair and trustworthy. The guidance was issued at the request of the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade to support consistent standards across the sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used in the training and development of AI systems. It evaluates the impact of this practice on creators, users, and the broader technology industry.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a formal response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, outlining its stance on the topic. It emphasises the need for stronger regulation, increased research investment, and international cooperation to harness AI’s benefits while mitigating its risks.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of the committee that will review how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards. It also provides a FAQ section to clarify key questions about the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written testimony to the Science and Technology Committee on how AI should be governed. The submission outlines the organisation's perspective on regulatory frameworks and ethical considerations for AI development and use.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy outlines how AI technologies will influence the rules that govern medical products. It explains how to apply the principles from the AI White Paper to ensure safe, effective, and trustworthy use of AI in healthcare.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This policy outlines a plan to make the Defence organization the world's most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI entity among nations of similar size. It focuses on deploying AI technologies to enhance defence capabilities, improve operational efficiency, and build credibility.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to take advantage of AI technology and boost innovation. It also sets up measures to identify and manage the risks that AI could pose to safety, privacy, and the public.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report updates how copyrighted materials are used to train and develop AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines current practices, challenges, and recommended actions to ensure lawful and ethical use of copyrighted content in AI development.
